correctness.rationale: The unique common-neighbor horizontal pair proves all 6n free-face collapses for n>=3. Explicit six-cycle links, connectedness, orientable diamond quotient and Euler 0 prove the nonexceptional cases are tori; n4 has an independently regenerated 18-step free-group attaching cancellation with one one-cell and six trivial two-cell relators. Complete verifier reconstructs every finite critical incidence for n=3..18, including exact n4 attaching words.

originality.rationale: The primary Shukla theorem covers the cyclic subfamily and the n4 garland type, but its hypotheses require a circulant. The noncyclic n divisible by 3 cases are not inferred. The indexed lattice-quotient torus theorem assumes period >=5, excluding period3, and the K_m-by-cycle result assumes m>=4. Prior exact rook computation is about relative high homology, not full homotopy. Remaining risk: unindexed equivalent classification.
residual_risks: Shukla already covers cyclic factors and an exceptional garland form; those are not independently new.
No exhaustive universal source index exists; an earlier unindexed theorem could include all noncyclic 3-divisible lengths.
No independent review and no equivariant homotopy statement.

value.rationale: This resolves a natural complete one-parameter short-period boundary family and exhibits a sharp exceptional n4 change from orientable torus to a circle joined to six two-spheres. It adds infinitely many noncyclic cases to existing classification methods and explains the topological transition by a precise link collision and 1-2 cancellation.
